title: Herbivore population/trait fields (C-027, Track A)
simLoop: First `populations` Process (SIMULATION_MODEL §3.7), registered across two bands like vegetation/vegetationSeasonal: pop.herbivore.density/stage.juvenile/stage.adult/occupancy/trait.limbLength/trait.webbing/swap.webbing on annual, pop.herbivore.trait.insulation on seasonal. Capacity is recomputed every annual step from a home-range-averaged read of veg.biomass.herb x habitat.suitability (never stored, ES-006). traitMean += traitRate*(pressureOptimum-traitMean)*dt, envelope-clamped; traitRate derives from this step's own stage turnover, never a hand-tuned constant. limbLength <- terrain slope, insulation <- climate.airTemperature, webbing <- tidal hydroperiod (NS-008) -- three real-world referents. Mismatch between the raw (unclamped) pressureOptimum and the envelope-clamped trait mean feeds an added mortality term, so a population that cannot meet a place's demand declines instead of morphing past its envelope. Grazing contributes a density-proportional mortality-rate term into veg.biomass.herb (C-027 §4.6.3) -- zero density is an exact no-op.
gameLoop: A herbivore population appears wherever there is forage and suitable habitat, its limb-length and coat visibly drifting to match the terrain and climate you carved -- leggier on rugged ground, shaggier after a cold snap -- and a population that has outgrown what the place can give it declines rather than cheating its way past the species' own limits.
notebookSeed: The herd here has gone shaggy since the cold set in.
tierO: D-007 clip verdict outstanding -- owner judges whether a herbivore population's limb-length/insulation/webbing trait-means visibly drifting after a force-dial change, and a population failing against its envelope in a place that has stopped suiting it, reads as legible earned adaptation or an arbitrary game effect. Ask filed: docs/playtests/A1-herbivore.md. This is the D-007 gate for every later Track A slice registering a new Process -- not a batchable Tier-O question.
